title: Challenge: connect containers on a user-defined network
intro: On Docker's default bridge, containers can only reach each other by IP. Create your own network and they get automatic DNS by name. Wire up two containers and prove it. (Commands are checked, not executed.)

steps.instruction: Create a user-defined bridge network named 'appnet'.
steps.success:
f3a9c1b2d3e4...
a new bridge network 'appnet' is ready

steps.instruction: List the networks to see it alongside the defaults.
steps.success:
NETWORK ID     NAME      DRIVER    SCOPE
1a2b3c4d5e6f   appnet    bridge    local
7g8h9i0j1k2l   bridge    bridge    local
3m4n5o6p7q8r   host      host      local

steps.instruction: Run a detached 'db' container (use redis) attached to 'appnet'.
steps.success:
9f8e7d6c5b4a...
db is up and joined to appnet

steps.instruction: From another container on 'appnet', reach 'db' by NAME (not by IP).
steps.success:
PING db (172.18.0.2): 56 data bytes
64 bytes from 172.18.0.2: seq=0 ttl=64 time=0.071 ms
the name 'db' resolved automatically, no IP needed
steps.fail: docker run --rm --network appnet <image> ping -c1 db  (reach it by container name)
steps.hint: docker run --rm --network appnet alpine ping -c1 db

steps.instruction: Inspect 'appnet' to see which containers are attached.

done: Solved! A user-defined network runs an embedded DNS server, so containers reach each other by name (db, web) instead of brittle IPs. That's the foundation Compose builds on for you automatically.
